english.title: Remove goods chargeable with a duty which was unpaid from place of importation with intent to defraud HM
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[removed]_
(B)_[assisted in the removal of]_
(C)_[were concerned in the removal of]_

goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..), chargeable with a duty which had not been paid, from

(D)_[their place of importation]_
(E)_[an approved wharf]_
(F)_[an examination station]_
(G)_[a transit shed]_
(H)_[a customs and excise station]_

at **(..SPECIFY THE PLACE OF REMOVAL..), with intent to defraud His Majesty of duty
english.legislation: Contrary to section 50(2)(b) and (4) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex
